描述_ZN: Scroll of "The Running Horse Raising its Mane", modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 41.4 cm in length and 52.3 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "Jusheng Shiren, brother and lady of the Jiali. Congratulation written by Beihong in August of 2007." Inscription: "Jiangnan Clothier" in vermilion and "Xiucai Renren" in white.　　Thirty-seven years that refers to the Republic of China 37 years (1948), Xu Beihong was 53 years old.　　From the inscription, we know that this picture is Mr. Xu Beihong to Ju Sheng and a woman's wedding congratulatory gift. As he did not know the woman, he was unable to inscribe the name of the lady.　　The picture depicts a horse in high spirits, galloping freely in the vast expanse of the earth and sky. Xu Beihong is particularly known for his paintings of horses among his animal subjects. Among his thousands of painted horses, all of them, with the exception of "Jiu Fanggao" painted in 1931, are horses without any restraint: no cage on their mouths, no saddle blanket on their backs, no shepherd or rider beside them. They are wild, untamed, unrestrained, sincere symbol of the god of freedom in Xu Beihong's mind.　　This painting is a late work of Xu Beihong, the rough and concise brushwork is not only in line with the anatomical principles of Western painting, but also contains the rhythm of traditional Chinese painting. The smooth inking portrays the horse's skeleton, muscles, and fur in an exquisite manner; the spontaneous and unrestrained shape fully expresses the horse's suave and unrestrained personality.
